flow_title: Write off small balances and deactivate dormant customers
flow_summary: A nightly run writes off small, long-overdue open invoices, but stops and undoes everything if more than 1,000 would be written off. A separate script marks customers inactive when they have had no invoice for 36 months.
flow_purpose: Clean up balances too small to chase and customers who no longer trade. The business team states small old balances are written off; the reason for deactivating customers is not known from the code.
starts_when: The nightly write-off procedure is run with a run date; the customer script is run on its own, with no trigger shown in the code.
outputs: Invoices marked written off, with the write-off date
Error 'too many write-offs' when the cap is exceeded
preconditions: The run date is supplied to the write-off procedure.
Invoices and customers exist in the accounts receivable tables.
flow_questions_for_sme: Who or what starts the nightly write-off and the customer script, and at what time?
Is the customer script meant to be part of the nightly run, and is its result saved afterwards?

flow_steps.text: Nightly write-off starts with a run date
Write off small open invoices overdue over 90 days
Did the update finish without error?
Failed: changes undone, error passed on
Mark active customers with no invoice for 36 months inactive

scenarios.title: Small old balances written off
when: Open invoices with a balance up to 2.50 are more than 90 days overdue.
scenarios.outcome: Qualifying invoices are marked written off with the run date and the change is saved.

steps: A: 1.80 is above 0 and at most 2.50; due 2026-07-01 is before 2026-07-15, so A qualifies
B: 2.51 is above 2.50, so B is left open
Count written off = 1, not above 1,000, so changes are saved
example.result: Invoice A: status W, write-off date 2026-10-13. Invoice B unchanged.

scenarios.title: Too many write-offs, run rejected
when: More than 1,000 invoices qualify for write-off.
scenarios.outcome: All write-offs from this run are undone and the run stops with an error.
scenarios.user_sees: Error -20001 with the text 'too many write-offs'.

steps: Changes are undone and the error is raised
example.result: No invoice is written off; error 'too many write-offs'.

scenarios.title: Database error during write-off
when: Any error occurs while the write-off runs.
scenarios.outcome: Changes are undone and the original error is passed to the caller.
scenarios.user_sees: The original database error; its text is not known from the code.

steps: The same error is raised again
example.result: No invoice is written off; the caller receives the error.

scenarios.title: Dormant customer marked inactive
when: The last invoice is more than 36 months before today.
scenarios.outcome: The customer's status is changed from active to inactive.

steps: Customer is active, so it qualifies

requirements.text: The system shall write off an open invoice when its balance is above 0 and at most 2.50 and its due date is more than 90 days before the run date.
The system shall mark a written-off invoice with status W and the run date as its write-off date.
The system shall undo all write-offs of a run and raise the error 'too many write-offs' when more than 1,000 invoices would be written off.
The system shall undo all write-offs of a run and pass the error on to the caller when any error occurs during the write-off.
The system shall mark an active customer as inactive when the customer's last invoice date is more than 36 months before today.

rules.title: Write off small old open invoices
rules.what_it_does: Marks open invoices as written off when the balance is small and the invoice is more than 90 days past its due date, then saves the change.
rules.business_reason: Small old balances are cleaned up because they are not worth collecting. Stated by the code comment 'Nightly clean-up of small balances' and the business team notes.
when_it_applies: The due date is before the run date minus 90 days.
rules.how_it_is_calculated: No calculation. Cut-off due date = run date - 90 days. Status becomes W and write-off date becomes the run date.
exceptions: An invoice due exactly on the cut-off date is not written off.
A balance of exactly 2.50 is written off.
questions_for_sme: What currency is the 2.50 limit in, and is it right for every customer and region?
Should the 90 days count from the due date as the code does, or from the invoice date?

rules.title: Cap of 1,000 write-offs per run
rules.what_it_does: If more than 1,000 invoices were written off in one run, undoes them all and stops with the error 'too many write-offs'. Otherwise saves.
rules.business_reason: Not known from the code. It may protect against a wrong mass write-off.
when_it_applies: More than 1,000 invoices were updated by the write-off.
rules.how_it_is_calculated: No calculation. The count of updated invoices is compared with 1,000.

values_used.name: Invoices written off in this run
values_used.value: Number of rows updated by the write-off

exceptions: Exactly 1,000 write-offs is allowed and saved.
questions_for_sme: Why is the cap 1,000, and what should happen when it is exceeded: who is told and how are the invoices handled afterwards?

rules.title: Any error undoes the write-offs
rules.what_it_does: If any error happens during the write-off, undoes all changes of the run and passes the same error to the caller.
rules.business_reason: Not known from the code. It keeps invoices from being left partly written off.
when_it_applies: Any error occurs while the write-off procedure runs.

values_used.name: Error
values_used.value: The error raised by the database or by the cap rule

steps: The same error is raised to the caller
example.result: No invoice written off; caller receives the error

rules.title: Deactivate customers with no invoice for 36 months
rules.what_it_does: Changes the status of active customers to inactive when their last invoice is more than 36 months before today's date.
rules.business_reason: Not known from the code. The business team notes do not mention this behaviour.
when_it_applies: The last invoice date is before today minus 36 months.
rules.how_it_is_calculated: Cut-off date = today's system date minus 36 months. Status A becomes I.

example.result: Status changes from A to I

exceptions: A customer with no last invoice date is never deactivated.
Customers already inactive are not changed.
questions_for_sme: Is deactivating dormant customers intended, and why 36 months? The change is not saved by this script: who saves it?
Should customers with no last invoice date also be deactivated?

glossary.business_meaning: Invoice status: O = open, W = written off
Balance still owed on the invoice
Date the invoice was written off
Customer status: A = active, I = inactive
Date of the customer's last invoice
